proof_skeleton_nl: Construct the bipartite graph whose edges are valid one-coordinate increments from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}. Instead of the false lexicographic reduction from the rejected attempt, introduce a new admissible-transfer partial order on K_{m,g}. A corrected compression lemma says every subset can be replaced by a same-size lower ideal with no larger neighborhood, and a separate hard lemma proves Hall's inequality for all such lower ideals. Hall's theorem then yields the desired injective map.

steps.derives: For the fixed integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, the one-coordinate increment relation between K_{m,g} and K_{m,g+1} defines a finite bipartite graph G_{m,g} whose left part is K_{m,g} and whose right part is K_{m,g+1}.
Let A be an arbitrary subset of the left vertex set K_{m,g}. To verify Hall's condition for G_{m,g}, it is enough to prove the inequality |N_{G_{m,g}}(A)| >= |A| for this arbitrary subset A.
steps.trivial_justification: Hall's condition is exactly the universal statement that every subset A of the left side satisfies |N(A)| >= |A|.

steps.derives: By L2, the admissible left-transfer relation <=_tr on K_{m,g} is a genuine partial order: it is reflexive and transitive by construction, and antisymmetry follows because every admissible left-transfer strictly decreases the weight omega(x)=sum_{r=1}^{m-1} r x_r. Therefore the notion of a lower ideal for <=_tr is well-defined.

Apply the corrected compression lemma L3 to the arbitrary subset A from A2. This produces a subset I of K_{m,g} such that I is a lower ideal for the transfer order <=_tr, |I|=|A|, and |N_{G_{m,g}}(I)| <= |N_{G_{m,g}}(A)|.
Because I is a lower ideal for the transfer order, L4 applies and yields |N_{G_{m,g}}(I)| >= |I|.

From A4, one has |N_{G_{m,g}}(A)| >= |N_{G_{m,g}}(I)| because |N_{G_{m,g}}(I)| <= |N_{G_{m,g}}(A)|. From A5, one has |N_{G_{m,g}}(I)| >= |I|. Again by A4, |I|=|A|. Combining these three facts gives |N_{G_{m,g}}(A)| >= |A|.
Because the subset A was arbitrary, the conclusion of A6 shows that every subset of the left vertex set K_{m,g} satisfies Hall's inequality in the graph G_{m,g}.
steps.trivial_justification: This is direct universal generalization from the arbitrary subset A fixed in A2.

steps.derives: Apply Hall's theorem L5 to the finite bipartite graph G_{m,g}. Since A7 establishes Hall's condition on the left side, there exists an injective function f:K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1} such that each x in K_{m,g} is adjacent in G_{m,g} to f(x). In particular, f is an injective map from K_{m,g} into K_{m,g+1}.

Set J_{m,g}=f. Therefore, for the given integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, if K_{m,g} denotes the set of all tuples x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that x_1+...+x_{m-1}=g and for all i,j in {1,...,m-1} one has x_i+x_j >= x_{i+j} when i+j < m and x_i+x_j+1 >= x_{i+j-m} when i+j > m, and K_{m,g+1} is defined analogously with coordinate sum g+1, then there exists an injective function J_{m,g} from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}.
steps.trivial_justification: This is just renaming the injective function f produced in A8.
